items.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: So I left and went with Joe Williams to play the blues.

ctx.x: That’s marvelous. And of course we’re filming this at our college, and I’m glad that students are hearing this, that it takes a combination of those skills. Tell us when you first started working with Sonny Rollins.

I worked with Sonny, starting I think in 1959 or ‘60. Sonny — I played the first Playboy Jazz Festival. And I met Sonny before around Chicago, but I never worked with Sonny, usually Victor Sproles or different bass players who were a little older usually worked with Sonny, and who were more established. And one day Sonny heard Walter Perkins the drummer and I, who, we came as a package you know. We worked a lot of jobs at the London House and different places on the off nights for Oscar Peterson, and people like…

it was really a very funny situation ‘cause it was in the afternoon on a Sunday afternoon. Sonny Rollins told us to be there I think the concert maybe started at one o’clock or two, I think about two. Sonny said well be there, ready to play at one. I get there, and we don’t see no Sonny. Two o’clock comes, the concert starts, the first group plays, fifteen, twenty minutes. The second group, fifteen or twenty minutes. The third group was a Dixieland band. And we were the fourth group to go on. The Dixieland band…
